status_taxonomy.active: At the ledger evidence cut-off, the defect is present and its affected path or control is usable; no verified repair is recorded.

defects.title: Instance-lock namespace and continuous ownership were not proved

incident.evidence: The final local source audit established the path-following, namespace-replacement and same-descriptor re-acquisition gaps without a network, provider or X action; no production concurrency incident, duplicate post or state race was established.
incident.explanation: This is a latent critical runtime defect present in the observed production lineage and the unactivated ee7539c candidate, repaired by the unactivated 2ad0f79 evidence cut-off. It is not evidence that two production processes actually posted concurrently.

defects.summary: The instance lock was opened through normal path-following file APIs and acquisition did not require one ordinary filesystem link or bind the acquired descriptor to a stable path identity. Later checks compared the held descriptor with the pathname and re-applied flock on the same open file description; after an accidental unlock that operation can reacquire the lock instead of proving continuous ownership. Normal remote-operation preflight therefore did not independently prove that the daemon still owned the single lock namespace shared with supported offline reconciliation.
defects.impact: A symbolic, aliased or replaced lock pathname can create a second lock namespace, and an unlocked daemon descriptor can reacquire rather than expose the ownership loss. A daemon, second process or offline reconciler could then proceed under different or unproved lock ownership and undermine receipt, schedule and ambiguity-marker mutual exclusion.

introduced.explanation: Commit f0be0b5 introduced the process-lifetime file lock using a pathname-following open and without a stable single-link acquisition identity; its parent 4f268ed contains no instance-lock implementation. Git ancestry proves f0be0b5 is an ancestor of both the observed production baseline be882e81 and the ee7539c evidence cut-off, where the defect remains.

defects.title: Fresh-process marker observation did not establish a blocking in-memory barrier

incident.evidence: Independent fresh-process fault injection reproduced a path to the local historical-context remote boundary with every network/provider operation replaced by a sentinel. No production, provider or X action occurred.
incident.explanation: The defect was reproduced in the unactivated 2ad0f79 candidate. It establishes an open remote-write barrier after restart, not an observed production post or duplicate.

defects.summary: A restarted process could observe a valid pre-existing ambiguity marker with both process globals initially false. If the marker disappeared during parent-directory fsync, acknowledgement failed and marker-durability uncertainty became true, but the incident latch remained false and neither direct preflight nor the scheduler treated uncertainty as blocking.
defects.impact: The marker could be the sole restart-surviving barrier, yet after its disappearance the fresh process could proceed to historical-context or another remote-write lane because the remaining in-memory uncertainty was not consulted.

introduced.explanation: Commit 2ad0f79 made marker acknowledgement fail on namespace disappearance and set marker-durability uncertainty, but fresh-process discovery did not seed the incident latch and the uncertainty flag was not part of the global blocking predicate. Earlier candidates had a different false-acknowledgement defect tracked by DEF-0032, so no predecessor is asserted as globally safe.
